title: High-Throughput Log Processing & Alerting Daemon in Go with Ring Buffers
problem: Production cloud applications generate tens of thousands of unstructured log events per second that quickly saturate network bandwidth, overwhelm centralized observability databases, and delay incident alerting. Naive log forwarders cause high CPU utilization, memory leaks from unbounded queueing during network partitions, and dropped critical alert signals. This project implements a high-throughput, low-latency log processing and alerting daemon from first principles in Go. The daemon reads high-volume log streams over stdio and Unix sockets into bounded circular ring buffers, parses structured attributes using optimized regular expressions, detects sliding-window error rate anomalies using Redis, and dispatches bulk indexing batches to Elasticsearch with backpressure control.
use_cases: Container host sidecar daemon parsing microservice logs and filtering noisy debug outputs locally
Real-time security anomaly monitoring detecting sudden spikes in HTTP 401/403 credential attacks
Observability pipeline ingesting high-throughput application logs into centralized search clusters
hard_parts: Managing bounded lock-free circular ring buffers to eliminate memory allocation churn during log surges
Optimizing regular expression tokenizers to parse structured attributes without creating CPU bottlenecks
Tracking sliding-window error rate anomalies across millisecond buckets with bounded Redis storage
Implementing backpressure and exponential backoff retry buffers when downstream Elasticsearch clusters saturate
screener_signals: Clean Go implementation cleanly separating ring buffer readers, Grok/regex parsers, Redis anomaly detectors, and bulk dispatchers
High-throughput load benchmark sustaining greater than 75,000 log lines/sec on a standard 4-core CPU with memory < 65MB
Anti-fake verification script streaming sudden dynamic fatal error bursts and asserting immediate anomaly threshold alert trigger

components.name: Bounded Ring Buffer Ingestion Daemon
components.purpose: Consumes raw log byte streams over stdio/sockets into pre-allocated memory ring buffers with zero allocations

components.name: Structured Regex Log Parser
components.purpose: Tokenizes raw lines into timestamp, severity level, service name, and message payload structures

components.name: Sliding-Window Anomaly & Alert Engine
components.purpose: Tracks error counts in sliding time buckets and triggers alerts when threshold breaches occur

components.name: Elasticsearch Bulk Indexer with Backpressure
components.purpose: Batches parsed logs into bulk HTTP requests, managing worker pools and backpressure rate limits

architecture.data_flow: Application log streams arrive over stdio or Unix sockets; the Ingestion Daemon writes lines into pre-allocated circular ring buffers; worker goroutines pull lines and execute optimized regex tokenization into structured log events; the Anomaly Engine updates Redis sliding-window error counters; if error rates cross configured thresholds, an alert dispatches immediately; parsed events accumulate in memory batches of 500 items; the Bulk Indexer flushes batches to Elasticsearch via HTTP; if Elasticsearch slows down, backpressure throttles ingestion buffer intake.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Bounded circular ring buffers dropping lowest-severity debug lines during persistent downstream backpressure; atomic Redis counters.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a high-throughput log processing daemon in Go with ring buffers, regex parsing, Redis sliding-window alerts, and Elasticsearch bulk flushing.
worksheet.q2: Target users: platform engineers, SREs, and observability infrastructure developers.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: container sidecar log filtering, real-time security anomaly monitoring, and central log aggregation.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 28 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 24 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 27.6 -> 28 hours. Intermediate level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: bounded lock-free ring buffers, regex optimization, sliding-window Redis error counters, and backpressure buffer management.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 500,000 log lines totaling 85MB across JSON and Nginx formats. Synthetic logs only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: local file indexer and in-memory Redis mock.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: GC latency pauses during high allocation. Fallback: sync.Pool buffer reuse.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: mock alert triggers. Anti-fake check 5 injects dynamic fatal error token at runtime and asserts alert message references token.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; synthetic log streams only.
